Subject: Re: Fwd: Reconciliation request: batch posting on 2026-08-24 (VAT split evidence)

Vanessa / Laura — I dug into the posting logs and annotated vat_breakdown_EMEA.xlsx (sheet: allocation_notes). Summary:

- Posting logic: when a single payment references multiple open invoices, we perform a proportional allocation based on invoice outstanding amounts at the time of sweep. VAT is calculated per invoice using the invoice’s billing country code stored on the invoice metadata.
- Edge case: if an invoice lacks a country code, we default to the customer account country (BrightByte HQ = GB), which caused two invoices to receive GB VAT rates.
- Rounding: we allocate VAT to pennies and then push any residual rounding difference to the earliest invoice in the batch.

I’ve added a column "source_payment_ref" in the CSV that maps to our ledger posting id (ledger_post_20260824_117). I can also pull the SWIFT trace — ops has to request it from the bank; estimate 24-48 hours for that.

Suggested response: share the CSV and the annotated Excel, and note the two invoices defaulted to GB because of missing country code. Offer the SWIFT trace if they need bank-level evidence (and ask for a short NDA if necessary).

(Attachments referenced: vat_breakdown_EMEA.xlsx [annotated], remittance_batch_20260824.csv)

Marcus Lin
Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com

Subject: Re: Reconciliation request: batch posting on 2026-08-24 (VAT split evidence)

Emily — thanks for the patience. Attached are the files we discussed: remittance_batch_20260824.csv (export from our posting engine), vat_breakdown_EMEA.xlsx (annotated with allocation rules and a per-invoice VAT column), and a one-page statement PDF. Key points below:

- Allocation: Redwood used proportional allocation across open invoice balances at time of sweep. VAT amounts are calculated per invoice using the invoice-level country code; two invoices defaulted to GB when country code was missing on the invoice metadata.
- Residuals: rounding residuals (under a £0.05 threshold) were applied to the earliest invoice in the batch. We documented the specific adjustments in the "notes" column of the spreadsheet.
- Payment reference: bank reference = RB-WIRE-824-EMEA; ledger posting id = ledger_post_20260824_117.
- Bank trace: we can request an intermediary SWIFT trace from our bank if BrightByte’s auditors require it (estimate 24-48 hours; may require a short request form).

If you want, we can schedule a 20-minute call tomorrow to walk your AP through the sheet. Otherwise, let us know if the annotated Excel suffices for your records.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Sales Lead | Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com | +1 415-555-0198
